headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad tool access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is elevated by TREK’s sensitive travel data handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP, while TREK exposes files, WebSocket/OIDC/MCP surfaces and runs in a collaborative session. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path if TREK content is fed into Cline or vice versa. The pathway is not proven by docs, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK content is copied into Cline prompts or files without sanitization
IF either agent consumes the other’s file output as instructions via MCP or workspace files
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of shared files into prompts
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Add a manual review step before any MCP-fed content is executed
Prefix untrusted content with explicit non-instruction markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys; TREK touches reservations, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets. If they share a filesystem or workspace, sensitive travel data can flow into Cline and then out through its third-party model calls. The blast radius includes secrets and reservations, so high fits.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace or exported files
IF Cline sends shared file contents to its model provider during normal operation
mitigations: Keep TREK secrets out of any shared workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Redact confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets before handoff
Turn off or restrict Cline access to sensitive directories
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem, modify git state, and execute shell commands; TREK is collaborative and uses files plus WebSocket/OIDC/MCP surfaces. If both operate on the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes and state changes can collide and corrupt code or travel data. The shared filesystem concurrency model makes this a default-dangerous overlap.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF TREK and Cline run concurrently without locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git locks or serialized commits
Restrict one agent to read-only access
requires-engineering: add workspace locking and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser actions, and file edits; TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in and can act on documents, reservations, and user-account data. If TREK treats Cline’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect travel actions or persisted bad state. The interaction is plausible and the downstream blast radius is broad.
conditions: IF TREK ingests Cline-generated text, code, or plans without verification
IF Cline’s outputs are used to update reservations, documents, or account data
mitigations: Require human review before TREK acts on Cline output
Add validation against source data before writes
Limit Cline output to suggestions only
Log and diff all downstream changes
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: TREK handles highly sensitive travel and identity-adjacent data, including API keys and MFA secrets, while Cline is a coding agent with broad network egress and model-provider API usage. If the pair processes EU PII or secrets in a shared workspace, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The evidence is docs-only, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF EU PII or secrets are placed into a shared workspace
IF Cline’s provider or logs retain data longer than TREK’s policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cline prompts and files
Review retention settings for both systems
Separate environments for travel data and coding tasks
Minimize logging of secrets and identifiers
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
